speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing; could you describe exactly what happens during these spells, how long they last, and if there is any loss of bladder control or tongue biting?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status (likely due to Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy or Lennox-Gastaut Syndrome).

The presence of a "muddy taste" (gustatory aura) and hand gestures strongly suggests complex partial seizures (focal seizures) with secondary generalization rather than typical absence seizures. To confirm this, I need to see the brain activity. REQUEST IMAGES: EEG (Electroencephalogram).
